system_requirements.requirement: The product shall be delivered as a responsive web application backed by a versioned HTTPS API that a mobile client can reuse later.
The web client shall support the latest two major versions of Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox, on desktop, tablet and phone screen sizes.
The product shall run on a managed cloud platform with automated instance replacement; a single availability zone is acceptable at this availability target.
The application tier shall be stateless and horizontally scalable behind a load balancer; session state shall live in a shared store, never on an application server.
A managed relational database shall be the system of record; object storage shall be used for any generated or uploaded files.
Separate development, staging and production environments shall exist, provisioned as code, with a CI/CD pipeline that runs automated tests and supports rollback within minutes.
Automated database backups with point-in-time recovery shall be kept, meeting an RPO of 24 hours and an RTO of 8 hours; a restore shall be tested at least quarterly.
Application performance monitoring, centralised structured logs, uptime checks and alerting on the availability and latency targets in this document shall be in place before launch.

Every third-party integration (email/SMS, payments, analytics) shall be called through an adapter with timeouts, retries with back-off and a circuit breaker, so a provider outage degrades one feature instead of the whole product.
Environment configuration shall be external to the code, and secrets shall be held in a managed secrets store, never in the repository or client bundles.
All timestamps shall be stored in UTC and displayed in the user's time zone; text shall be stored as UTF-8 to allow later localisation.

security_requirements.requirement: Passwords shall be stored using a modern adaptive hash (Argon2id or bcrypt), be checked against known-breached passwords, and be at least 10 characters; login shall be rate-limited with temporary lockout after repeated failures.
security_requirements.verification: Security review and automated test of the login flow

security_requirements.requirement: Multi-factor authentication shall be available to all users and mandatory for administrators and any user role that can access other people's data or payouts.
Sessions shall use short-lived tokens with rotation, secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies (web), server-side invalidation on logout and password change, and an idle timeout.
Access shall be enforced on the server for every request using role-based permissions, with object-level checks so one user can never read or change another user's records by changing an ID.
security_requirements.verification: Automated authorization tests per role; penetration test

security_requirements.requirement: All traffic shall use TLS 1.2 or higher with HSTS; plain HTTP shall redirect and internal service-to-service traffic shall also be encrypted.
security_requirements.verification: TLS scan (e.g. SSL Labs grade A)

security_requirements.requirement: Databases, backups and object storage shall be encrypted with AES-256; keys shall be managed in a key-management service and rotated at least annually.
The product shall be protected against the OWASP Top 10: parameterised queries only, output encoding, CSRF protection, a strict Content-Security-Policy and standard security headers.
Public endpoints shall have rate limiting and bot/abuse protection (sign-up, login, password reset, search and any messaging or review submission).

Security-relevant events (logins, permission changes, admin actions, data exports, deletions) shall be logged with user, time and origin, protected from modification, and retained for at least 12 months; logs shall not contain passwords, tokens or full payment details.

Dependencies shall be scanned on every build, critical vulnerabilities patched within 7 days and high within 30 days, and an independent penetration test performed before launch and at least annually.

Applicable data-protection law for the launch geography (for example GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA or the India DPDP Act) shall be identified before build; the product shall record consent where required and support access, correction, export and deletion of a person's data.
security_requirements.verification: Legal review; test of the data-request flows

security_requirements.requirement: Each data category shall have a documented retention period, and expired or deleted personal data shall be removed from the live system and from backups within a defined window.
A written incident-response plan shall define roles, escalation, evidence handling and breach notification to users and regulators within the legally required time.
Production access shall be limited to named staff on a least-privilege basis, require MFA, and be logged; no shared accounts.
Every vendor that processes user data shall be assessed and covered by a data-processing agreement before integration.

Card data shall never touch or be stored on the product's servers: payments shall use a PCI DSS-compliant hosted payment provider, webhooks shall be signature-verified, and payment actions shall be idempotent to prevent double charges.

epics.name: Authentication & Account Management
epics.description: Provides secure account creation, login, and session management so that Customers and Providers can access role-appropriate functionality. This module is the entry point that gates every authenticated action elsewhere in the product.

epics.name: User Profile Management
epics.description: Lets Customers and Providers maintain the personal and account information the product needs to operate correctly — contact details, preferences, and (where relevant) payment or payout details.

epics.name: Search & Discovery
epics.description: Helps a Customer find the right Service quickly through search, filtering, and browsing, translating an open-ended need into a short, relevant list of Services to choose from.

epics.name: Service Catalog
epics.description: Maintains the authoritative set of Services a Provider offers, including descriptions, pricing, media, and availability status, so Customers always see accurate, up-to-date listings.

epics.name: Booking & Checkout
epics.description: Lets a Customer commit to a Service — selecting details, reviewing cost, and confirming — and turns that intent into a tracked Booking record that both sides can rely on.

epics.name: Scheduling & Availability
epics.description: Manages when a Service can actually be delivered — Provider availability windows, slot capacity, and conflict prevention — so a Customer only ever sees and books slots that are genuinely open.

epics.name: Payments & Billing
epics.description: Handles the movement of money for every Booking — capturing payment, tracking its status, issuing refunds, and keeping a reliable financial record for reconciliation.

epics.name: Provider Management
epics.description: Covers how a Provider joins the platform, gets verified, and manages their standing — the supply side of the marketplace that makes Services available to Customers in the first place.

epics.name: Reviews & Ratings
epics.description: Captures Customer feedback after a Booking completes, giving future Customers a trust signal and giving Providers (and Admins) a feedback loop on quality.

epics.name: Notifications
epics.description: Keeps every party informed of state changes that matter to them — Booking updates, account events, and operational alerts — through the right channel at the right time.

epics.name: Customer Support & Help
epics.description: Gives a Customer or Provider a way to get help and gives Support staff the tools to resolve issues — from self-service help content to a tracked ticket when something needs a human.

epics.name: Admin & Operations Console
epics.description: Gives internal Operations and Admin users the tools to run the platform day to day — managing users, Services, and Bookings, and stepping in when something needs manual attention.

epics.name: Reporting & Analytics
epics.description: Turns raw product activity into the numbers the business needs to run itself — Booking volume and revenue for Finance, activity and quality metrics for Operations, and usage trends for Product.

epics.name: Security & Access Control
epics.description: Ensures that every action in the product is performed by an authorized party and that sensitive data is protected — the cross-cutting layer every other module depends on.

epics.name: Onboarding & Activation
epics.description: Guides a newly-registered Customer or Provider from account creation to their first successful core action, so the value of the product is obvious quickly instead of requiring them to figure it out unassisted.

epics.name: Privacy, Consent & Data Retention
epics.description: Gives users control over their own data — requesting a copy of it, deleting their account, and managing consent for optional data uses — and ensures the platform actually enforces its stated retention policy rather than only describing one.
